attempts.paper_title: Transcranial Focused Ultrasound Modulates Feedforward and Feedback Cortico-Thalamo-Cortical Pathways by Selectively Activating Excitatory Neurons
attempts.entry_title: Ultrasound modulation of cortico-thalamo-cortical pathways (Gao et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Gao, Ramachandran, Yu and He (2025) on transcranial focused ultrasound of rat S1. Dandiset 000463 cites the paper but holds only broadband S1 recordings of four other rats, without units or trial times, so the claims are tested on the paper's own deposit, dandiset 000946. Its units are not typed as RSU or FSU, so only the auditory cortex claims can be tested, the unit counts and the responses to five PRFs.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Gao et al. (2025) from dandisets 000463 and 000946

outcomes.statement: The analysis of Figure 4 rests on 312 RSUs and 54 FSUs from S1 and 233 RSUs and 17 FSUs from POm in the 3000 Hz PRF sessions, and on 148 RSUs and 61 FSUs from S1 and 189 RSUs and 43 FSUs from POm in the 30 Hz PRF sessions; Figure 6 pools 1050 RSUs and 247 FSUs from S1 and 913 RSUs and 106 FSUs from POm over the five PRFs.
outcomes.source: Figure 4 legend; Figure 6 legend
outcomes.quote: There are 312 RSUs and 54 FSUs recorded from S1, 233 RSUs and 17 FSUs recorded from POm for PRF 3,000 Hz. There are 148 RSUs and 61 FSUs recorded from S1 and189 RSUs and 43 FSUs recorded from POm for PRF 30 Hz. ... sorted 1,050 RSUs (A) and 247 FSUs (B) recorded from S1 ... sorted 913 RSUs (C) and 106 FSUs (D) recorded from POm
outcomes.notes: The paper's deposit DANDI:000946 holds sorted units and trial tables for these sessions, but every unit's celltype_label is 0 (the column says 1 is RSU and 2 is FSU), 33 recordings have no such column, and no waveforms are deposited, so the RSU and FSU types the claim needs (Methods, Neuronal type classification, k-means on each spike's IP and AHP) cannot be assigned. The criterion compares counts by type, so none of the 12 can be compared. Untyped, the constant-PD series of the 10 subjects with POm recordings holds 320 S1 and 339 POm units with more than 2000 spikes at 3000 Hz (paper, RSU plus FSU, 366 and 250), 390 and 315 at 30 Hz (209 and 232), and 1630 and 1429 over the five PRFs (1297 and 1019), leaving out the one recording whose copies are labelled both S1 and POm. Since RSU plus FSU is the untyped total, both counts of a region and condition can be within 10% only if the total is within the sum of their ranges; that fails in all six groups, so at most 6 of the 12 counts could match under any typing. The claim therefore cannot be reproduced, but whether it is partially (6 to 9) or not reproduced depends on the types, so it stays blocked. The sorting itself is the paper's (units are deposited); it is not redone.

outcomes.quote: During sonication, the AC neurons showed time-locked responses to 1,500 Hz (n = 107, p = 9.9 × 10−5) and 3,000 Hz PRF (n = 104, p = 1.98 × 10−7). Postsonication, neuronal responses were activated by 30 Hz (n = 83, p = 1.77 × 10−20), 1,500 Hz, (n = 107, p = 1.36 × 10−5), 3,000 Hz (n = 104, p = 4.47 × 10−13), and 4,500 Hz (n = 100, p = 1.66 × 10−40)
outcomes.notes: 633 AC units of the constant-PD series, none dropped. Under O2a, Kruskal-Wallis across PRFs p = 7.8e-6 during sonication and 5.2e-49 after it; mean normalized rates during 105.9, 99.7, 140.3, 107.1 and 108.0% at 30, 300, 1500, 3000 and 4500 Hz, after 176.4, 94.3, 147.9, 310.5 and 210.8%, so 300 Hz is lowest in both windows. 1500 and 3000 Hz are significant during sonication and 30, 1500, 3000 and 4500 Hz after it under every O3 and O4 reading (6 of 6 named results), and 300 Hz is not significant after it. But 4500 Hz is also significant during sonication under all six O3 and O4 readings (corrected p 2.4e-6 to 0.009), 30 Hz under three and 300 Hz under the two O3b readings, where the claim has only 1500 and 3000 Hz responding. Under O2b every mean, the -134 to -67 ms baseline included, is 54 to 74%, the during-sonication Kruskal-Wallis test gives p = 0.021, and at most 2 of the 6 named results hold (not reproduced). Session means vary widely (1500 Hz 99 to 302% during sonication; 3000 Hz 112 to 654% after it). With every AC session at these PRFs (all PDs) the outcome under O2a is also partial and 300 Hz is not the lowest. Leaving out any one of the six subjects gives partially reproduced or reproduced under every O2a reading, never not reproduced. Under the claims file's header a claim whose method readings disagree is blocked; O2a is adopted as an assumption because O2b does not put no change at 100%: on synthetic Poisson units without a stimulus effect O2a gives 99.9 to 101.6% at 2 to 40 Hz and O2b 13, 31, 77 and 127% at 2, 5, 15 and 40 Hz. Whether O2b should stay a reading is asked of a reader (questions/000463.yaml). Question for the paper's authors (finding): how was the normalized rate formed, the ratio of mean counts or the mean of per-trial ratios.
deviations: Tested on the paper's deposit DANDI:000946 (`data: elsewhere`), constant-PD series of the AC group, 6 subjects (the paper reports 12 rats in the AC group) and 633 units where the paper has 453.

Assumed the normalized rate is the mean count in the window over the mean count in the 67 ms before onset (O2a). The Methods say only that the rate 'was normalized to 67 ms before each stimulation'. The other reading (O2b, mean of per-trial ratios) puts an unchanged window near 60% where the paper's scale has 100% for no change (sham and control p = 1.0, responses reported at 123 to 159%), so O2a is the reading the paper supports. On synthetic Poisson units with no stimulus effect O2a gives about 100% at every rate and O2b 13 to 127% depending on the rate (notebook). Under O2b the claim is not reproduced; both are shown.

Sessions are the constant-PD series, from the Methods, Transcranial focused ultrasound stimulation, paragraph 3 ('For the PRF effect exploration, the pulse duration (PD) was set at 200 μs for all the PRFs'); every AC session at these PRFs is shown as a variant.
Sonication onset is the trial start_time, as the files' general/stimulus says; the notebook shows the population rate rising at it and not at times shifted by 1 s.

findings.statement: Dandiset 000463 cites this paper as its detailed description, but holds none of the recordings the paper analyses. Its 29 files are 32-channel broadband and LFP recordings of one S1 probe from rats BH395, BH396, BH401 and BH444 (November 2022 to February 2023), with intensities given in volts in the identifiers; the paper's deposit, dandiset 000946, has 19 other subjects recorded from August 2023, two areas per recording and mostly 500 trials per recording (691 of 814; the others 400 to 499). None of the paper's claims can be tested on 000463.

The files of 000463 have no units, no trials or epochs table and no stimulus series, so the sonication onsets and the conditions' trials cannot be read; the conditions appear only in the identifiers (for example BH401_3000_200_67_5V, BH396_test5_24V). The description says 200 or 500 trials per recording; the recording lengths give 121 to 515 intervals of 2.5 s.
In 000463 every electrode's location is 'unknown' and the electrode group's location is the placeholder 'brain area', so the recorded area is not stated.

In 000946 the units table's celltype_label column is described as 'label 1 = RSU, label 2 = FSU', but all 22599 values in it are 0 (each recording counted once), and 33 recordings have no such column. No waveforms or waveform measures are deposited, so the RSU and FSU types, on which 31 of the 37 claims rest directly, cannot be recovered.

Most recordings of 000946 are deposited more than once under different file names: of 1550 spike files, 728 recordings have two copies, 2 have three and 1 has four (same trial table, spike counts and first and last spike times); 84 have one.

In 000946 one recording, BH499_300_200_67_5_POM_S1, has identical spikes in two files noted 'Recording:S1' and two noted 'Recording:POM', so at least one area label is wrong and that session's other area may be missing; the attempt leaves it out of all counts.

000946 holds no sham sessions and no sessions targeted at CG1, the paper's control (Figure 5), and not the hydrophone scans of Figure 1C. It holds M1- and POm-targeted sessions and PRF series at 300, 1500 and 4500 Hz that the paper does not describe.

The AC group of 000946 has 7 subjects and the subjects with POm recordings number 10, where the paper reports 12 and 16 rats. The constant-PD AC sessions hold 633 units with more than 2000 spikes where the paper reports 453, and each PRF count is higher; which sessions and units the paper used is not documented.

Question for the paper's authors: is the normalized spiking rate the mean count in the window divided by the mean count in the 67 ms before onset, or the mean over trials of per-trial ratios? fig11b-ac-prf-responses is partially reproduced under the first and not reproduced under the second; the attempt assumed the first. Also, is 'against baseline' a rank-sum test against the prestimulation window (all 100%), against another window, or a signed-rank test against 100%, and is the Bonferroni factor the number of windows or of parameter levels? These did not change the outcome here.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The executed notebook of the author run with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the paper. The verifier was given the claims file of dandiset 000946 (claims/000946, 33 claims) where this attempt is written against claims/000463 (37 claims), so its claim ids, readings and criteria are those of the other file; its results are mapped here to this file's claims. methods-insitu-pressure and fig11-ac-unit-counts have no counterpart in its file, and the verifier gave no outcome for them. Its other points: the duplicate recording labelled both S1 and POm is now left out from all counts; spike times are checked to be in increasing order in every loaded file (none is out of order); the S1 and POm counts are broken down by subject and PRF.

disagreements.reason: The RSU/FSU split can't be tested, but the criterion's partial clause needs only the per-area totals, which don't depend on typing. Cell 16: 3000 Hz S1 320 vs 366, POm 339 vs 250; 30 Hz S1 390 vs 209, POm 315 vs 232. None is within 10%. For the Figure 6 counts, untyped totals over five PRFs: S1 1648 vs 1297 (+27%), POm 1429 vs 1019 (+40%), both outside the 10% the partial clause allows, under any typing.

With the claims file's readings (N1/N2 x B1/B2, Bonferroni C1 = x5), cells 20 and 21 give: N1/B1 partial (during 1500, 3000 and 4500; 4500 is one extra); N1/B2 not reproduced (during adds 300 and 4500, two extras); N2/B1 and N2/B2 not reproduced (KW during p = 0.021). The readings disagree and none reproduces, so it is blocked as methods_underspecified. judge() applies the wrong partial rule (kw_ok and sum(named) >= 4 against the file's sets differ by one PRF in one window), never applies the header rule that disagreeing readings make the claim blocked, requires 300 Hz lowest in both windows where the file says at least one, uses Bonferroni x2, which is not a reading in the file, and lets O3c, which is not the file's B3, decide outcomes. The N2 reading is biased by firing rate: on synthetic Poisson units with no stimulus effect it gives about 33%, 89% and 121% at 5, 15 and 40 Hz.

entries.name: 000463-gao-2025
entries.title: Ultrasound modulation of cortico-thalamo-cortical pathways (Gao et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Gao, Ramachandran, Yu and He (2025) on transcranial focused ultrasound of rat S1. Dandiset 000463 cites the paper but holds only broadband S1 recordings of four other rats, without units or trial times, so the claims are tested on the paper's own deposit, dandiset 000946. Its units are not typed as RSU or FSU, so only the auditory cortex claims can be tested, the unit counts and the responses to five PRFs.
